title: Biolistic Transfection in Euplotes crassus
author: Angela Piersanti
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zk6f4ze
materials: Shooting conditions were set as follows in the Bio-Rad Biolistic PDS-1000/He Particle Delivery System : rupture disk 1550 psi, helium pressure 1750 psi, vacuum 26 inches Hg, gap distance ⅜ inches, 1st shelf.

steps.title: Prepare cells on HEPES‑soaked filter
steps.instruction: Place 10^5 vegetative Euplotes crassus cells, or 10^5 mating DP1 and DP3 strains (50 h after mixing), onto a filter paper that has been soaked with 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Biolistic shooting with gold nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Shoot the cells on the filter using golden nanoparticles of either 0.6 µm or 1.6 µm diameter that have been coated with 1.25 µg of the construct containing the G418 resistance gene.

steps.title: Recover cells in seawater
steps.instruction: Fold the filter paper after shooting and place it into 50 mL of seawater; note that >50 % of the cells remain alive after transfection.

steps.title: Apply G418 selection
steps.instruction: Begin antibiotic selection 24 h after transfection, adding G418 at increasing concentrations every 4 days, starting at 1 mg/mL and progressing up to 10 mg/mL.
